phases.message: I'm Marguerite Aldous. This is my mail: my office manager's note, a scan of a California letter, a note from my field lead, an offer from a claims firm and an email from an employee. Read every message. Don't answer anything yet: I'll send you to my HR, my files and the three states' sites.
This is my HR, Crewmarrow. Read my people, every page, and look up Gideon Park. Don't do anything yet.
This is Binderwell, my personnel files. Read every page. Don't do anything yet.

This is Brazenhall, the Texas desk. Read its rules and my five notices. Answer, contest or report each notice that is open and should be, with the facts and the evidence, by its id, and leave out the ones that should not. Then tell me what you did and why.

This is Sutterwick, the California desk. Read its rules and my notice. Also answer the California letter that came only by post (CA-2, in my mail) here, by its number. Answer or contest each as the facts and the date allow. Then tell me what you did and why.

This is Evergale, the Washington desk. Read its rules and my three requests. Answer, contest or report each one that should be, and leave out the ones that should not. Then tell me what you did and why.
Back to my mail. Give me the list of all ten notices: what you did with each, and the dates I must not miss.

tx.text: Brazenhall Notices (Texas), an invented desk that applies Texas's rules to Ketterby Survey Group's notices. Topics: deadline, response, separation, charges. The open notices are in read_notices. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

An employer has 14 calendar days from the date the desk mails a notice to respond, counted from the mailing date on the notice and not from the day it arrives. A response inside the 14 days makes the employer an interested party, who is sent the determination and may appeal it. After the 14 days the desk takes no response: the employer is not an interested party and has no right to appeal that determination. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

A response gives the dates worked, the reason for the separation, any extra pay, and the facts: the final incident, prior warnings, the policy and witnesses. One response is taken for each notice; a notice that has been answered is closed to a second. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

A layoff for lack of work is not a reason to disqualify: it is answered with the facts and not contested. A quit without good cause, or a discharge for misconduct, may disqualify; an employer that says so gives the evidence, such as the resignation, or the warnings and the policy the worker signed. A notice about a person who never worked for the employer is answered by saying so, not as a separation. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

Benefits paid on a claim are charged to the employer's account. Under the federal rule (26 U.S.C. 3303(f)) a state must not relieve an account of charges for a payment made because the employer failed to respond timely or adequately, when the employer has a pattern of such failures. The maximum potential charge of each notice is in read_notices. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

ca.text: Sutterwick Claim Desk (California), an invented desk that applies California's rules to Ketterby Survey Group's notices. Topics: deadline, response, separation, wages. The notice on this site is in read_notices; a notice that came only by post can be answered here by its number. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

An employer has 10 days from the date printed on the notice to respond, counted from that date and not from the postmark or the day the letter arrives. A response after that loses the written decision and the right to appeal. The same date applies to a notice that came only by post. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.
A response gives the dates worked, the reason for the separation, the pay, and the facts. One response is taken for each notice. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

A layoff for lack of work is answered with the facts and is not contested. A discharge for misconduct is contested only with the evidence: the final incident, prior warnings and the written policy. An employer with no warning and no policy on file states that it has none and does not allege misconduct. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.
A claimant who still works part-time has wages to report. The employer states the hours and the pay since the claim date, so that the desk can reduce the benefit. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

wa.text: Evergale Separation Desk (Washington), an invented desk that applies Washington's rules to Ketterby Survey Group's requests for separation information. Topics: deadline, adequate, claims. The requests are in read_notices. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

The due date is printed on each request for separation information. After the due date the desk decides on the information it already has, and the employer has to appeal the decision; failing to respond can affect the tax rating. No response is taken as a separation answer once the due date has passed. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

A response is adequate when it gives accurate information of sufficient quantity and quality that a reasonable person could decide whether the claimant is eligible (RCW 50.29.021). A pattern of untimely or inadequate responses is three in the previous two years, or 20 percent of the employer's current claims, whichever is greater. A layoff for lack of work is answered with the facts. A discharge for misconduct is contested with the final incident, the warnings and the signed policy. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.

A claim filed in the name of a person who still works for the employer is not a separation. It is reported to the desk as a claim filed fraudulently, and it is not answered as a separation. The employee is told to report the identity theft herself. Today is Friday 9 October 2026.
